CONFIRMED REAL. The quoted formula appears verbatim at line 42 of the Domain facts, and `wisdom_bonus` (like `monster_multiplier`) is never defined anywhere in the document — not in the Domain facts, which define every other term of that formula numerically (max level 50, the TOTAL four-band level_penalty table, +5 HP/+2 slots per level, the 100-turn cap), and not in any clause. A whole-spec search for the settling clause finds exactly one other mention of wisdom: S-020's "the projected wisdom bonus, which scales every award equally and so is selected once per rung under a ranking purpose." That fixes only WHEN it is chosen and that it is monster-independent; it never fixes its VALUE, and a factor of 0 scales every award equally just as a factor of 1 does. S-007 demands the value be "derived from game data" and forbids "a constant", but supplies no wisdom-stat-to-bonus mapping — if anything it cuts against A's invented `1 +` and `/100` as much as against B. No clause forbids output B. Both are legal under every clause. The hole is in fact wider than the exhibited pair — with the symbol wholly undefined any value is legal, and it multiplies the sole reward term the entire walk is driven by.

Note first: no spec path was supplied to me in this dispatch, so I could not open the Domain-facts/S-clause document; per my instructions I did not go looking for it. My judgement rests on the witness's own account of what the spec does and does not say, plus the arithmetic, which I re-derived independently (1000/22 kills x 39/10 fights = 1950/11 = 177.2727..., ceiling 178 — branch A is internally coherent).

Taking the witness's account at face value, this is a real gap and a severe one under the user-impact lens.

1. The omission is asymmetric and therefore not a stylistic quibble. The Domain facts pin down level_penalty as a TOTAL table, and give max level, per-level grants and the turn cap as literal numbers — i.e. the spec's own convention is that every factor in the award formula gets a definition. wisdom_bonus and monster_multiplier are the two factors left as free symbols in that same product. A reader who honours the spec's convention has nothing to read them off.

2. S-007 turns the omission into a genuine fork rather than an obvious fill-in. If the spec forbids substituting a value not derived from game data, then quietly writing 1 for an undefined factor is exactly the substitution S-007 bans; and 1 + wisdom/100 is equally invented — nothing in the spec chooses /100 over /10 or /1000. So branch A is not "the obviously intended reading that any implementer would pick"; it is one of several unsanctioned inventions, and the witness's B ("wisdom_bonus is the bonus wisdom confers, which for wisdom 0 is 0") is a literal reading of the identifier's own name. Two implementations both satisfy the written spec.

3. The divergence is catastrophic, not cosmetic. Under B the product is Round(0) = 0 for EVERY admissible monster, S-013's zero-reward stop fires, and the walk returns rungs=[] with +infinity — level 25 is reported UNREACHABLE. Under A the same input returns 178. That is not two shades of an estimate; it is "the planner works" versus "the planner declares the game unwinnable and refuses to act."

4. It fires on the common case, not an edge case. wisdom 0 is the default state of a character with no wisdom-bearing gear, i.e. most characters for most of their early and mid life. So B does not misprice a rare corner — it zeroes the objective for the modal input, and does so silently, because +infinity is a well-typed answer that reads as "correctly determined to be impossible" rather than as an error. An operator watching a level-24 character sit idle while the tool insists level 25 cannot be reached would absolutely file a bug, and would be right to: the failure is indistinguishable from a genuine content wall, which is the worst kind of wrong answer this system can give.

5. Nobody could shrug either way. There is no reading on which "every monster in the catalogue awards zero XP, therefore leveling is impossible" is an acceptable alternative outcome to "178 cycles." This fails the don't-care test decisively — one branch is a total functional failure, so the spec must say which one it means.

Fix required of the spec: define wisdom_bonus and monster_multiplier explicitly as functions of named game-data fields (including their value at wisdom 0), or state outright that they are multiplicative factors defaulting to 1 and carve that default out of S-007. The monster_multiplier omission is the same defect and should be closed in the same edit.

REAL. Both quotes are verbatim (S-015 ¶4-5, lines 377/379; S-020 line 514-515), and the spec never classifies which side of its own state/loadout split the wisdom_bonus term of the published award formula lives on.

QUOTE FIDELITY. S-015: "The projected state's OWN attributes are given by a closed formula and by nothing else." and "**Gear never enters that formula, in EITHER direction.** A piece the re-evaluated loadout adds does not raise the projected maximum, and — this is the harder half — a piece the re-evaluated loadout DISPLACES does not lower it either. The formula's only inputs are the handed total and the number of levels gained." S-020: "One quantity is deliberately NOT per candidate: the projected wisdom bonus, which scales every award equally and so is selected once per rung under a ranking purpose." Both exact, both in context.

WHY NEITHER CLAUSE FORBIDS THE OTHER'S OUTPUT.
- S-015 does not forbid B. Its closed formula is stated only over PUBLISHED PER-LEVEL GRANTS: `handed_maximum + G × (k − L0)` "where `G` is the published per-level grant, and likewise for every other published per-level grant". The Domain facts publish exactly two per-level grants (+5 max HP, +2 inventory slots); wisdom is not among them, so the formula has no G for it and the "gear never enters" sentence is written about "the projected maximum" specifically. The spec elsewhere treats the projected state and the loadout as two DISTINCT objects handed to consults — S-010: "the projected rung state (S-015) and the monster, with the loadout S-020 constructs" — so a gear-derived quantity's living outside the closed formula is a shape the spec already uses. S-021 makes it a stated principle: "The maximum hit-point pool is a published per-level grant, so gear must not inflate it in either direction; the damage is a combat outcome, so it must be judged under the loadout the character will actually fight in." A gear-borne multiplier patterns with damage under that very principle, and no clause says wisdom is a "projected state OWN attribute".
- S-020 does not forbid A either — it presupposes loadout provenance ("selected", "under a ranking purpose") without ever stating it, so a reader who takes S-015's "and by nothing else" as a closure (attributes with no published per-level grant stay at the handed value) reads S-020's paragraph as merely fixing granularity. That reading leaves the paragraph near-vacuous, which is exactly the tension: each clause's plain reading makes the other's a dead letter, and no third clause adjudicates. Searched the whole document: "wisdom" appears only in the Domain-facts formula and that one S-020 sentence; S-007 fixes the formula and its rounding but names only "the catalogue's attributes for that monster" as the source, never the character-side term.

DIVERGENCE VERIFIED IN EXACT RATIONALS. Gap g = 10−5 = 5 → 70% band. Base ((5/10)·20 + 25·0.04) = 11; 11 · 7/10 · 1/25 = 77/250 = 0.308. A: S-007 half-up → 0, sole admissible monster awards nothing → S-013 stops the walk under S-012's rule → rungs = [], total = +infinity (S-012's "POSITIVE INFINITY, SPECIFICALLY"). B: ×9/5 → 693/1250 = 0.5544 → 1; S-023 rate = 1 XP per loop action (S-021's zero-damage case makes the loop a bare Fight), S-019 exact quotient 100/1 = 100 actions, S-020 setup 3/30 = 1/10 → rung 1001/10, S-014's single upward resolution of the total → 101. Both are legal complete walks; the divergence is not a price difference but REACHABLE against UNREACHABLE, which is the one error S-019 says "the objective cannot tolerate". The amulet's min_level 10 is satisfied at the handed level itself, so B needs no rung-unlock to fire — the flip is available on the very first rung.

Determinism is not the live axis (both arms replay identically); the load-bearing content is the provenance flip. Not a misquote, not out of context, not settled elsewhere.

REAL — and this is close to the worst shape a projection gap can take, because the two readings do not differ by a few percent, they differ by REACHABLE vs UNREACHABLE.

The divergence. Both branches agree on everything except one question: when the walk projects an XP award at a rung, where does the wisdom bonus come from? A sources it from the handed state (S-015: wisdom is not a published per-level grant, gear never enters the projected state) → factor 1. B re-derives it from the rung's re-evaluated loadout (S-020), which at level 10 unlocks the carried amulet → factor 9/5. The witness's numbers are internally coherent: 693/1250 ÷ 77/250 = 1.8 = 9/5 exactly, so the award is linear in the bonus and provenance is the ONLY moving part. B's rung cost also checks: 100 loop actions + 3/30 setup = 1001/10, resolving upward to 101.

Why it is not a don't-care. The observable outputs are `rungs=[], total=+infinity` versus `rungs=[('chicken', 1001/10)], total=101`. That is not two acceptable answers to the same question — it is the difference between the objective pricing a level-target route at 101 cycles and discarding the entire branch as impossible. Downstream of J, +infinity is absorbing: no competing route ever loses to it, so the whole leveling arm silently disappears from ranking. A finite 101 competes normally. There is no ranking in which those two are interchangeable.

The bug report writes itself, in both directions:
- Getting A when expecting B: "the planner says level 11 is unreachable while I am carrying an amulet, of the exact min_level I have just reached, that makes every chicken pay." An operator watching the bot sit on a full bag refusing to grind files that immediately. This is the more damaging direction, because +infinity does not merely mis-price, it removes the option and leaves no trace in the plan tree to debug from.
- Getting B when expecting A: the projection counts a bonus from a piece that is in the bag, not on the body, and prices the route on stats the character does not currently have. An auditor reconciling projected cycles against realized cycles finds a systematic optimistic bias with no visible cause. That is the classic already-done/not-yet-done confusion, and it under-prices every rung, not just this one.

Severity of the mechanism, independent of this witness's knife-edge. Yes, the specific flip here rides a rounding boundary — 0.308 vs 0.5544 straddles S-007's Round, and only there does the factor decide between award 0 and award 1, which is what arms S-013's every-admissible-monster-awards-nothing stop under S-012. One could dismiss the exhibit as measure-zero. That dismissal is wrong for two reasons. First, the provenance choice is load-bearing on EVERY rung of EVERY projection as a straight multiplier on the award; the rounding boundary is merely where it becomes catastrophic rather than merely inaccurate. Second, the catastrophic case is not rare in practice: it is exactly the low-level, early-gear, grey-adjacent regime where awards sit near the rounding floor and where a newly-unlocked carried piece is most likely to exist — the min_level 10 amulet at level 10 is the normal case, not a contrived one.

The spec-level fault. This is not silence, it is a collision: S-015 and S-020 both speak to the projected state and give opposite answers, with no stated precedence. A conflict is strictly worse than an omission, because each implementer can cite a clause and believe they conformed, and the acceptance suite passes for both. The gate that would catch it does not exist, since both readings are deterministic and idempotent — the witness explicitly replays the call and both branches are stable, so no flakiness or replay check will ever surface it. It will surface as a live behavioral mystery instead.

What the spec must say. One sentence fixing provenance: whether the projected wisdom bonus is frozen from the handed state for the whole walk, or re-selected per rung from a re-evaluated loadout — and if the latter, whether carried-but-unworn pieces count and whether the S-020 setup movement is charged. Absent that sentence, the zero-reward stop in S-013 is not determined by the spec, and neither is reachability.

Caveat on my confidence: I was given no spec file path and did not read one, so I cannot confirm S-015 and S-020 are quoted faithfully. If a precedence rule exists elsewhere in the document that the witness overlooked, this collapses to a reading error rather than a gap. Everything I can check — the arithmetic, the coherence of both branches, and the decision-relevance of the divergence — holds, and the impact if the witness is right is severe enough that the 5/5 blast radius is justified rather than inflated.

The divergence is a genuine value-semantics split, not a labelling or structural one. A returns rungs=[] with total = positive infinity — which S-012 fixes as the specific value meaning "target not reached, no number of actions is claimed" and which "orders above every finite cost". B returns rungs=[(cow, 100)] with total = 100, a finite reported count of executed planner actions under S-004/S-014. These are different values on the same declared output shape (S-003: an ordered rung sequence plus a total cost): different length of the rung sequence, and a finite total against the spec's designated unreachable sentinel. Any consumer that compares totals — S-012 explicitly contemplates an argmin/ordering over candidate totals — sees the candidate as reachable in one implementation and permanently unreachable in the other. That is the maximal end of "value semantics", not naming, field labels, formatting, or ordering of an unordered collection.

The two are also not the same behaviour described twice: they disagree about which monster crosses the rung, whether a rung is crossed at all, and whether the walk terminated under S-013. The witness's arithmetic is internally coherent on the given inputs — damage 0 for both monsters means S-021 contributes nothing and the loop is the bare Fight, so the S-023 loop-action denominator is 1 and S-019's exact quotient 1000/10 gives exactly 100 loop actions, an integer that S-014's upward resolution leaves untouched. Chicken's gap of 14 puts it in the g>=10 zero band, so A's S-013 stop is equally coherent.

The underlying silence that admits both is real: S-002 enumerates only out-of-range levels and duplicate monsters as MALFORMED, so an observation naming a monster with no catalogue row is not excluded from the domain; S-011 quantifies over "the monsters admitted by S-009 and S-010", i.e. the background predicates, never over the catalogue's key set, so nothing in the text says catalogue membership is what makes a monster a candidate; S-018's presence test (one kill, positive rate, a carried level) is satisfied by cow and mentions no catalogue requirement; and S-017's restatement ratio at two identical levels is a self-ratio that one reading resolves to 1 by identity while another cannot form at all without the catalogue attributes S-007 would need. The "catalogue's completeness" residual explicitly declines to settle which monsters appear in the catalogue, which leaves exactly this seam open rather than closing it. Neither branch is plainly illegal on the text, so the difference is admitted by the spec and observable on Σ's value-semantics dimension.

SCOPE verdict: REAL — the divergence is owned by the artifact under test.

The artifact is "ONE pure function — the cycle oracle" which is handed exactly four things (S-002): a character state, a target level, a body of learned observations, and the static catalogue. The disputed decision is: over WHAT universe does the oracle enumerate candidates at a rung — the catalogue's rows only, or the union of catalogue rows and monsters that appear in the observations? That enumeration happens inside the oracle's own body, between reading its inputs and consulting the background predicates. Applying the lens's literal test: if I implemented this function, could I make this choice? Yes — it is one line of my own loop, and the two answers A (rungs = [], total = +inf) and B (rungs = [(cow, 100)], total = 100) are both the oracle's own return value under S-003, not somebody else's output.

None of the carve-outs claims it:
- "The learning store's collection machinery — how observations are recorded, windowed, or aged" governs the PRODUCTION of observations. The oracle is explicitly said to *read* them. Once handed a cow entry, what the oracle does with it is the oracle's.
- "The beatability predicate itself" and S-010's engagement predicate are background only as to HOW they decide; S-009/S-010 say the clauses constrain "when and with what arguments the oracle consults it". Which monsters get offered to the predicate at all is precisely the "with what arguments" side, i.e. the oracle's side. The witness stipulates both predicates admit both monsters, so the divergence cannot be pushed into them.
- The progression choice core, the acquisition pricer, the planner/goal/arbiter are downstream consumers of a value that already differs at the oracle's return.
- The RESIDUAL "The monster catalogue's completeness … is the catalogue's concern, not this oracle's" is the closest carve-out, and it cuts the other way for this lens: it disclaims responsibility for what the catalogue CONTAINS while leaving the oracle to be total (S-001) over a body where an observed monster has no row. It disclaims a producer's duty, not the oracle's behaviour on the resulting input.

Nor is the input ruled out of the domain. S-002's malformed list is closed and specific — out-of-range current/target level, and a monster appearing twice in either body — and this body violates neither, so S-001's totality obligation still binds the oracle on it. That the mismatch is not declared malformed is what leaves the choice sitting inside the artifact rather than at its boundary.

(Separate note, not part of the scope verdict: the same input also pressures S-007's "over the catalogue's attributes for that monster" and S-017's ratio, which the witness routes around via the identity ratio at level 15. That is additional oracle-internal silence, not a reason to reassign ownership.)

REAL. The quote is verbatim in S-012 ("If at some rung no monster satisfies S-009 and S-010, the walk stops there.") and is exactly the clause whose universe is unnamed: it quantifies over "monsters" without saying which set is being filtered.

No clause in S-001..S-023 or the residuals states that a rung's candidate set is the catalogue's key set, and none declares an observation naming a monster with no catalogue row to be malformed. The evidence:

1. S-002's malformed-input list is only (a) a current or target level outside the legal range and (b) a monster presented twice. This body has neither, so S-001's totality obligation applies and the oracle must answer.
2. S-002's own emphasis licenses the mismatch rather than forbidding it: "EACH MONSTER APPEARS AT MOST ONCE IN EACH OF THEM" — at most once in EACH body, i.e. zero occurrences in one of them is admitted input. "Exactly once" was the available word and was not used.
3. S-011 ranks "among the monsters admitted by S-009 and S-010"; S-009/S-010 both defer to background predicates, and S-010 is expressly default-admit ("a monster is admitted unless those rules exclude it"), fixing only the arguments ("the projected rung state and the monster"). The set being filtered is never named.
4. S-007's catalogue dependence governs PREDICTION only, and S-008 supersedes prediction where a measurement is present. Cow's measurement is PRESENT by S-018's own test (40 recorded kills, positive rate, a level attached), so S-008's mandate ("uses that measured rate") reaches it by the letter.
5. The RESIDUALS entry on catalogue completeness is the only nearby text and is explicitly undecided — "none may be treated as settled" — so it cannot forbid B.

The strongest candidate forbiddance, S-017's "Where the published award at the level the samples were taken is not positive ... the restated rate is zero", does not fire: cow's published award is not non-positive, it is UNDEFINED (the formula needs monster_level and monster_hp, which no row supplies). Treating a nonexistent value as "not positive" is itself an unlicensed interpretive move, and even that reading still admits cow as a candidate and reaches +infinity by a third route (rate 0 -> S-013), which multiplies the non-determination instead of closing it. B's arithmetic is clean under the letter: sample level 15 = rung level 15, so S-017's ratio is award(15)/award(15) = 1 by identity with no catalogue attribute needed; S-023 keeps the rate in XP per loop action, S-019 gives the exact quotient 1000/10 = 100 loop actions, S-014 rounds the total once (already whole).

I built both readings as pure total functions and ran them on the stated input: reading A (universe = catalogue keys) returns ([], +inf); reading B (universe = every monster identity the inputs name) returns ([(cow, 100)], 100). Both honour every clause; the divergence is unreachable/infinite versus reachable-at-100, which is decision-changing for any consumer.

REAL (severity high). Note first: no spec path was given in my brief, and I am forbidden to enumerate directories to hunt for one, so I judged the witness's clause citations (S-002/S-008/S-013/S-017/S-018) as presented, on their own terms, under the user-impact lens. I read no source, tests, or fixtures.

Why it is a real gap and not a don't-care:

1. The two readings are not two shades of the same answer — they are "unreachable" vs. "100 actions". +infinity is an ABSORBING value in a ranking objective: a route priced at infinity is not merely deprioritized, it is eliminated, and every other route wins by default. A finite 100 is a route the planner will actually commit a character to. There is no interpolation between them and no downstream clamp that makes them interchangeable.

2. Both branches are load-bearing on a domain the spec (per the witness) never names. A enumerates candidates FROM the catalogue; B enumerates them from the background admissibility predicate and then prices via the measurement path. B's chain is the stronger of the two precisely because it never needs a catalogue attribute at all: S-018 says the measurement is present (one kill, positive, carries a level), S-008 mandates using it, and S-017's restatement ratio collapses to 1 by identity when the recording level and the target rung are the same level 15. So the measurement path can price a monster the catalogue has never heard of, without ever noticing it is missing. That is the signature of an unnamed universe, not of an under-specified edge case.

3. S-002 makes the input WELL-FORMED. If an observation for an uncatalogued monster were malformed, the whole question would be a validation error and no gap would exist. The witness's point is that S-002 enumerates out-of-range levels and duplicate monsters and stops there — so this input must be given an answer, and the spec supplies two.

4. The input is realistic, which is what makes it bug-report-shaped rather than academic. Catalogue and observation stores are keyed independently and go out of sync in exactly this way: a cached/filtered catalogue slice, a renamed or reseasoned content code, a monster observed on a map the catalogue snapshot predates. This repo's own history is full of key-mismatch defects of that shape.

5. A user files a bug under EITHER outcome, and which one is "correct" depends on a fact the spec does not record. If cow is genuine, A silently discards 40 real kills' worth of evidence and reports a reachable level as impossible — the operator sees a character that will not advance while its own log shows it earning XP. If cow is stale, B prices a phantom route at 100, wins the ranking with it, and the character stalls at execution against a monster it cannot find — and the stall is far from the decision that caused it. Both are filed. That is the opposite of a don't-care carve-out: a don't-care is when nobody cares which way it goes, and here the safe answer depends on provenance the spec never asks anyone to supply.

The missing clause is not "handle cow". It is two named things: (a) the candidate universe for a rung — catalogue rows, admissibility-predicate extension, or their intersection; and (b) the disposition of an observation whose monster has no catalogue row — S-002-malformed, silently dropped, or admitted and priced measurement-only. Naming (a) alone still leaves (b) open whenever the universe is the intersection, because the observation is then live evidence with nowhere to attach.

Blast radius 5/5 is credible but slightly over-stated as a per-clause figure: the damage is confined to states where the observation store and the catalogue disagree. Within those states it is total, because infinity propagates unrecoverably into route ranking.
